headline: Corn ends the week at $4.56 as crude gains 3.8% to $103
lead: Corn closed Friday at $4.56, down 4½ cents, while beans added 3½ cents to $12.56½. Crude ran the other way, up 3.8% to $103.27 as Saudi-Houthi tension pushed Brent toward $120.
teaser: Corn slipped to $4.56 Friday while crude gained 3.8% to $103.27; cattle held near records.

one_number.unit: gap between soybean and corn prices, per bushel
one_number.context: Beans at $12.56½ and corn at $4.56 leave the widest gap in a while. That spread keeps acres arguing for beans next spring.

sections.title: Grains finish the week quiet
sections.body:
- Corn fell 1.0% to **$4.56**, a lower close, and beans added 0.3% to $12.56½.
- Wheat was flat at $6.25, and Friday's trade was a small-change session heading into the weekend.
- USDA admitted a data error in its September corn report, but the 181.2-bushel yield stays as published.
sections.so_what: Harvest supply is still the weight on corn, with no new buyer in sight.

sections.title: Cattle hold near highs
sections.body:
- Live cattle settled at **$229.88**, up 0.1%, and feeders gained 0.6% to $348.33.
- The October Cattle on Feed report showed September placements and marketings at the lowest in the series.
- USDA also changed its cash cattle reports, and the first screwworm find in US wildlife was confirmed in a Texas elk.
sections.so_what: Tight supply keeps cattle firm, while screwworm is a risk nobody can size yet.

sections.title: Crude climbs, gas drops
sections.body:
- WTI gained 3.8% to **$103.27** on Saudi-Houthi tension, and Brent is closing in on $120.
- The US is again drawing on its Strategic Petroleum Reserve, already at its lowest since 1982.
- Natural gas fell 5.6% to $2.64, near the bottom of its 52-week range.
sections.so_what: Crude is the one market moving hard, and farm fuel costs follow it.

outside_the_pit.title: Grain merchandisers face higher costs and margin-call risk
outside_the_pit.body: Bigger inventories, high freight and margin calls could strain working capital at elevators this fall.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress. Corn and bean harvest pace shows how fast supply is reaching the market.
Export sales. Weak soybean numbers would sit poorly beside China's 25 million ton pledge.
WTI above $103 and Brent nearing $120 would keep fuel costs rising into November.

source_summary: CME Group settlements, AgWeb, Feedstuffs, Beef Magazine, OilPrice, USDA

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.82 vs $4.62 projected (+4.3%), 17 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.74 vs $11.09 projected (+14.9%), 17 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Ours: the average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 23, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.84 and soybeans at $12.75, both through Oct 22. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 23. Oct 1-31 window, most states.
